title: Left a department, then named as an executive or owner of its contractor
question: Which former City employees are named, within three years of leaving, as chief executive, officer or owner of a firm or organization holding a contract with the department they left?
finding: 6 former employees with a rare name: 5 not in the older screens, 3 of them first named within a year of leaving. Their former departments have paid those 5 contractors $43.3 million since the first notice. A further 17 former employees appear only as unpaid directors, and 1 common-name pair: counted, not listed.
how: Payroll names that stop being paid by a department, matched to executives and owners (chief executive, finance or operating officer, principal officer, shareholder, owner) on later contract notices whose department contact is the department they left. The leaving date is the Form 700 leaving statement where there is one, otherwise the end of the last fiscal year paid. The Ethics Commission’s list of post-employment waivers is checked for each name.
limits: Moving from a department to an organization it funds is ordinary and often wanted by both. The City’s rules, as the Ethics Commission’s waiver page states them, bar a former employee for one year from contacting the old department to influence it, bar for one year employment by a party to a contract the person personally took part in awarding, and bar permanently switching sides on a matter the person worked on; none of those can be tested from these records. A principal officer named on a notice may hold a clinical or programme title rather than run the organization. Every row is a name match.
